about: What's new in Magic Merger, one line per merged update, newest first. Players read it in the ? menu. A builder adds a line in the same pull request (docs/DAILY.md); idea is the Ideas tab id the update built, when it came from one.

entries.text: Shields now stop meteors, fireballs and other thrown spells at their edge. A shield cracks as it takes hits and breaks under a stronger spell, or a second one of its own strength.

The island moves more smoothly: on phones that keep up it now draws 60 frames a second instead of 30, and creatures move on every one of those frames. A phone that cannot keep up goes back to 30 on its own.

People you create now join the island as real villagers: a Human moves into a house of the nearest village, takes a job and lives with a family there. A Blacksmith works the forge, a Necromancer walks among the graves at night and raises the dead, a Knight guards the village. New creatures are made as living things: a Serpent slithers and hunts, a Fox Spirit tends the woods.
A spell you cast is now saved two seconds after it lands, so reloading the page right after a cast no longer loses it.

Every item you discover from today is made as what it is, of seven kinds: a spell, a creature, an object, a building, a settlement, a place or land. A new settlement is a real village with houses, fields and villagers, a new temple or tower stands beside the houses at their size, and a new book stays the size of a book unless it is a giant's. Items found before today will be remade the same way, a few at a time.

Small fixes: messages no longer cover the tabs on a phone or repeat the same hint three times, new items on the board no longer land on top of each other, the order menu in Craft fits the screen, and the Community tab's favorite spell menu shows the spell you picked on another device.

A spell whose last rewrite failed its own test now gets one more try, told what went wrong the first time. Four are in the queue, one spell a day with the others: Wormhole Network, Protection Spell, Fountain of Youth and Void Familiar.

Spells caught breaking their promise are now written again, one a day: Frost Nova first, whose thaw set the village on fire, then Light, then spells that failed their own test. The new version reaches you only once it passes its test.

Spells that keep their own state now work as written (Starfall Rain heals and calms again), a refusal is no longer shown as an item's description, a wonder no longer names a friend who hid or left, and items found on the Community tab no longer count the eight forces.

Daily challenges: every night a new item waits to be found, and the first to make it has their name on it. A Community tab shows who plays and their favorite spell, and this list tells you what changed.
Your account's name sits in the top bar, and the spell bar in the World can be resized.
Accounts you can trust: sign in, sign out and switch on any device, and see when your progress last synced.
A library of nature that keeps growing: a new wonder each day, and your discoveries can appear on new islands with your name.
Wonders of nature on islands, and villages where no two houses are alike.
Nature that is never the same twice: plants, animals and villages that belong to their land.
The seed chooses the land, big islands mix several, and rivers wind.
Bigger and richer worlds: seven kinds of land, water that runs, and a better view.
Creatures move like they mean it: herds, flocks, packs and paths.
Faster creation: every new item is written the moment you merge it.
The review's findings fixed: safer accounts, votes and casts.
Accounts with passkeys: your progress follows you on every device.
Challenges from nothing, artifacts that act, and the island's own chronicle.
A living island: creatures with goals, villages, food, taming and memory.
Many kinds of life, each with its own body.
Spells keep their promise: a protection really protects.
The Ideas tab: post an idea, vote for others, and see Claude build them.
Play with friends, each with their own invite link.
Spells get better: vote on what a spell did.
The voxel island, spells written as programs, challenges, artifacts, day and night.
